source: 7de339b plus quiet-inputs (contract v5: scripted inputs raised at recorded service boundaries on DOS)

levels.2: passing isolated unit or differential tests
levels.4: verified against the original DOS executable in a stated domain (three-way, scenario level)

notes: Levels are the highest level reached inside the stated domain; a subsystem can be level 2 for isolated routines and still level 5 at scenario level. Both are given.

Scenario checks run natively against references recorded once per DOS executable (build/reference/, portable/tests/acceptance/step_check.py, seconds per scenario). Native replays each DOS run's own per-site clock values and its chronological service order (clock reads, BIOS keyboard samples, queue-count samples, pumps, simulation boundaries); each recorded input is admitted at its recorded service position through the ordinary SDL adapter. The canonical lane (native vs canonical DOS) tests the port, the original lane tests the whole chain. Verdicts are game state per DoAntSim entry. The handler-entry CX/DX a keyboard IRQ copies into its event (on DOS the wrapper's DGROUP residue) is replayed from the tape as part of the interrupt. Since contract v5 the DOS recorder holds each scripted input until the next recorded service boundary and raises it there, so native placement is exact; inputs arriving mid-raster (outcome depends on CPU speed) are outside the tested domain.
Open findings are pinned per lane in portable/tests/acceptance/known_findings.json; the upper-layer test fails on any change in either direction.
